absent: Full worker structure layout beyond flags, pool linkage and scheduler fields referenced here.
Work structure, delayed work and barrier layouts plus color and flag bit definitions.
Contracts of kick_pool, need_more_worker, worker_set_flags and pool management helpers.
Rescuer main loop, mayday timer handling and idle culling implementation.
Flush, drain, plug and color-advance transitions beyond field roles.
Unbound pool creation, hashing, refcounting and attribute handling.
Sysfs interface, lockdep integration and trace-point payloads.
Per-CPU pool tables, node active allocation and topology setup sequences.

findings.text: Pool object carries lock, cpu, node, id and flags plus progress timestamp and stall marker, running counter, pending worklist, worker totals and idle count, idle list with timer and cleanup work, SOS timer, busy hash, manager and last-woken hints, attached list, ID allocator, attributes, unbound hash node with refcount, RCU head and optional RT cancel lock.

Per-pool queue holds pool and wq back pointers, work_color and flush_color, refcnt, per-color flight array, plugged flag, nr_active with inactive_works list, pending_node, pwqs_node and mayday_node linkages, mayday_cursor marker, stats array, release_work and rcu with alignment tied to PWQ shift.

Queue object holds pwqs and list linkages, mutex, work_color and flush_color, nr_pwqs_to_flush, first_flusher with flusher_queue and flusher_overflow, maydays with rescuer, nr_drainers, max_active and min_active with saved copies, attrs with dfl_pwq, optional sysfs and lockdep state, fixed name, rcu, cache-aligned flags, per-CPU pwq table and per-node active table.

Flusher links via list, awaits flush_color and signals done; node accounting keeps max, atomic nr, lock and pending_pwqs; shard layout keeps nr_large_shards, cores_per_shard and nr_shards with derived default count; pod type keeps nr_pods, pod_cpus, pod_node and cpu_pod; off-queue data keeps pool_id, disable and flags; violation entry keeps func, atomic cnt and hash_node.
POOL_BH uses bit zero; POOL_MANAGER_ACTIVE uses bit one; POOL_DISASSOCIATED uses bit two; POOL_BH_DRAINING uses bit three.

WORKER_DIE uses bit one; WORKER_IDLE uses bit two; WORKER_PREP uses bit three; WORKER_CPU_INTENSIVE uses bit six; WORKER_UNBOUND uses bit seven; WORKER_REBOUND uses bit eight; WORKER_NOT_RUNNING combines prep, intensive, unbound and rebound.

WORK_CANCEL_DELAYED uses bit zero and WORK_CANCEL_DISABLE uses bit one; NR_STD_WORKER_POOLS equals two; UNBOUND_POOL_HASH_ORDER and BUSY_WORKER_HASH_ORDER equal six; MAX_IDLE_WORKERS_RATIO equals four; IDLE_WORKER_TIMEOUT spans five minutes; MAYDAY_INITIAL_TIMEOUT spans ten milliseconds with two-tick floor; MAYDAY_INTERVAL spans one hundred milliseconds; CREATE_COOLDOWN spans one second; RESCUER_BATCH equals sixteen; RESCUER_NICE_LEVEL and HIGHPRI_NICE_LEVEL use minimum nice; WQ_NAME_LEN equals thirty-two and WORKER_ID_LEN adds ten.

BH slice uses two milliseconds in jiffies with restart bound ten; WCI_MAX_ENTS equals one hundred twenty-eight; intensive threshold defaults to unsigned maximum, warning threshold defaults to four and shard size defaults to eight; affinity labels are default, cpu, smt, cache, cache_shard, numa and system; per-queue stats track started, completed, cpu time, intensive breaches, management wakeups, repatriations, maydays and rescued plus sentinel.

Associated pools keep workers bound to their CPU with concurrency management active and without unbound marking; disassociated pools mark every worker unbound, suspend concurrency management, permit execution on any CPU and behave as unbound pools.
Bottom-half pools exist per CPU and remain always disassociated because each CPU supports a single concurrent bottom-half execution context.

Running count rises in process context on the associated CPU with preemption held off and falls or resets in the same context while holding pool serialization, letting lock holders reliably detect zero.

A worker lives in busy hash, idle list or manager role; manager pointer is advisory; start decisions require idle presence and creation triggers when demand exceeds idle supply; idle reaping uses timer plus cleanup work under ratio and retention bounds.

Once active tally reaches queue limit, arrivals park on inactive list with inactive marking and stay outside active tally; every parked item carries marking while some marked barriers execute elsewhere; flush barriers stay exempt from active accounting and ordinary marking matches parking.
Issue and flush colors advance at pool and queue scope with per-color flight tallies and waiter plus overflow lists; plugged state pauses dispatch and drainer tally tracks draining.
Pool, per-pool queue and queue teardown use RCU to support lockless lookup, first-queue selection and global dumps; unbound per-pool release defers to a dedicated thread worker.

Pool serialization covers flags, progress time, pending list, worker totals, idle tally, idle list with timers, SOS timer, busy hash and manager hints, plus per-pool colors, refcount, flight tallies, plugged state, active tally, inactive list and mayday cursor.

Global pool mutex guards pools and queue registry and qualifies together with RCU for global iteration; attach mutex guards attachment, detached list walk and disassociated flips to avoid racing concurrent attach.

Queue mutex guards colors, flushers, drainers and saved limits; distinct annotations separate write-rare linkage, power attributes, node pending lists, rescue linkage and freeze state; RT adds a cancel lock for bottom-half workers.

Idle denotes availability, prep denotes entry into execution, intensive denotes long CPU holding, unbound denotes detached execution, rebound denotes returned workers and die requests exit; the not-running union withholds running-count contribution and gates scheduler handling.

Work items register with debug tracking using callback hint and static-bit test; setup separates on-stack from heap; active fixups synchronously cancel then re-register or release while other states refuse; delayed on-stack teardown stops its timer then releases tracking.

Tick adds advisory CPU time without locks, then elevates over-threshold managed workers to intensive and nudges the pool; per-callback breach counts warn first at threshold and again on exponential backoff; bounded table drops newcomers when full; empty builds no-op and zero threshold disables elevation.

Running notification clears sleeping state, conditionally raises running tally under preemption guard and restarts execution clock; sleeping notification raises sleeping state then under lock lowers tally and possibly wakes pool; tick notification updates stats and may elevate; last-callback query returns prior callback for a thread.

Lifecycle helpers initialize work and tear down delayed on-stack items; cursor callback exists solely as list position marker; iteration helpers traverse bottom-half and normal per-CPU pool pairs, global pool registry and attached workers under their required contexts.
Exports are __init_work, destroy_delayed_work_on_stack, wq_worker_running, wq_worker_sleeping, wq_worker_tick and wq_worker_last_func covering init, teardown, scheduler hooks and last-callback query.

Predefined queues are system_wq, system_percpu_wq, system_highpri_wq, system_long_wq, system_unbound_wq, system_dfl_wq, system_freezable_wq, system_power_efficient_wq, system_freezable_power_efficient_wq, system_bh_wq, system_bh_highpri_wq and system_dfl_long_wq, mostly frozen after init.
Mayday cursor must never dispatch; entry traps fatally.

Unbind may preempt between running-state test and tally update, so running path blocks preemption and sleeping path revalidates under lock; sleeping marker prevents duplicate tally drops and tick skips elevation while exiting.
Shared CPU-time tally is deliberately racy; breach lookup is lockless with locked insertion plus retry on race and quiet drop when table is full.

Startup gating uses wq_online and topology flag with read-mostly annotation, pwq_cache slab, pod tables with default cache-shard scope, online, unbound, requested and isolated masks with command-line seed and per-CPU round-robin cursor; debug force has true and false variants; standard and ordered attribute templates exist per pool kind; freeze flag, manager wait and update buffer coordinate suspend, management and attribute refresh.

Overload linkage parks per-pool queues on queue mayday list serviced by a shared rescuer at minimum nice; SOS timing escalates from initial delay to periodic interval and rescuer drains bounded batches while stats record maydays, rescues and repatriations.
Node scope caps active work via max with atomic tally and pending list of queues holding parked work; each queue carries a per-node table.
